title: KV/prefix-cache load harness: multi-metric regression detection and memory-pressure scenarios
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Implement a robust load-testing harness for KV and prefix cache behavior that measures tokens/sec, p95 latency, and memory footprint across varying cache hit rates and memory pressure. The harness will be used in CI to detect regressions that affect latency and throughput when cache hit ratios change or when memory budget tightens.
test_plan: 1) Generate synthetic traffic with replayed production prefix traces and parametric generators (zipfian, session-based prefixes). 2) Sweep cache hit rates: 20%, 50%, 80%, 95% via controlled trace selection and key aliasing. 3) Sweep memory budgets: nominal, -25%, -50% (simulate tighter node memory). 4) Measure tokens/sec, p95 and p99 latencies, GC/alloc profiles, and per-model KV memory. 5) Run 30 minute warmup + 60 minute steady-state for each cell. 6) Record metrics to bench DB and push dashboards and artifacts to CI job logs.
matrix: Workload axes: hit_rate=[20,50,80,95], sequence_length=[32,128,512], concurrency=[8,32,128], memory_budget=[100%,75%,50%], region=[us-west-2, eu-central-1]. Metrics: tokens_per_sec, p50_lat, p95_lat, p99_lat, evictions/sec, cache_entries, memory_bytes, token_cost_estimate.
instrumentation: Integrate with existing bench-exporter: add kvcache.detailed.metrics (hit_count, miss_count, eviction_count, prefix_lookup_time_ms), record client-side end-to-end latencies and server-side internal latencies (KV lookup, kernel exec, post-processing). Ship artifacts: flamegraphs, jemalloc stats, heap dumps (on failure), and per-run ndjson of sampled requests.
success_criteria: 1) CI job fails if p95 increases more than 15% vs baseline AND tokens/sec drops more than 10% for any hit_rate cell. 2) No memory leak across 2-hour run (RSS drift < 7% after warmup). 3) Regression detector flags run only when both latency and throughput regress simultaneously or when memory evictions exceed threshold (configurable).
results: (placeholder) initial canary runs completed on us-west-2 with 80% hit rate and memory_budget=100%: tokens/sec stable (~124k tokens/s baseline 128k), p95 increased 4%, evictions negligible. Observed one outlier on sequence_length=512 with p99 spikes tied to GC pauses; follow-up profiling ticket created.
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Prototype harness implemented using bench-runner v0.9; added replay loader for prefix traces (public-sanitized traces).
2026-03-08: Added param sweep and job templating for k8s batch runners; initial dashboards created in Grafana (bench/kvcache-15723).
2026-03-10: Ran three canary matrices; captured flamegraphs for p99 spike; raised ENG-15758 for GC investigation.
2026-03-13: Implemented dual-threshold regression detector (latency + throughput) and uploaded regression-detector prototype to CI pipeline.
notes: Design decision: require a simultaneous regression in both p95 and tokens/sec to reduce noisy false positives from transient network blips.
Trade-off: longer steady-state windows increase run time but reduce variance; we landed on 60 minutes steady-state as a compromise for CI patch runs vs nightly exhaustive runs.
Follow-ups: integrate with canary rollouts in console so failing benchmark cells can block a rollout for the affected model variant.
next_steps: 1) Harden artifact collection (rotate large artifacts to long-term storage). 2) Wire acceptance criteria into Jenkins/CI gating for runtime-1.20 branch. 3) Expand matrix to include quantized model variants and dedicated GPU pod shapes. 4) Schedule coordinated runs with SRE to validate autoscaler response under memory pressure.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (this sprint): CI canary integration for PRs touching kvcache or scheduler. Phase 2 (next month): nightly expanded matrix and alerts for persistent regressions. Phase 3: Console integration for pre-rollout checks (runtime-1.20).
